findings.reason: as written the executor either under-delivers ("every reader" still false for a resume) and passes its gate, or hits a scope refusal on a course-correction inside a file it was not granted, so the plan needs either `reckon/crew/resumption.py` in the write paths (or a stated in-scope re-resolution by project) or its claim narrowed to the dispatch path.
findings.text: §21's deliverable says `_persisted_worker_environment` "forwards the same mapping to `launch_search_path`", but its only cli-launch caller, `_supervisor_spec` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:2411`, calling `_persisted_worker_environment` at `:2459`), receives a `LaunchPlan` and no backend mapping — `LaunchPlan` (`reckon/_backends.py:394`) carries the backend as a name only — and `_supervisor_spec`'s own callers are `dispatch.py:3448` (which does hold the mapping) and `supervised_launch` (`dispatch_launch.py:2640`, reached from `:1626` and from `resumption.py:1534`), which hold only the plan; the resume and lane-change launches, whose `resolve_launch_executable` callers §21 itself names at `dispatch_sessions.py:1332` and `:1849`, therefore compose their persisted PATH through the same host-layer-only `backend_name` arm today and cannot carry the project-layer directory without editing `reckon/crew/resumption.py` (its local `_spawn` at `:1519`), which is not in §21's write paths; and the done-when cannot see the shortfall, because its first case asserts only a fresh dispatch's persisted PATH

response_events.note: LaunchPlan now carries the resolved backend search directories, computed at plan build where the project-resolved mapping is held, so _supervisor_spec, the resume path and the persisted environment all read them from the plan; reckon/_backends.py joins §21's write paths, and the availability report moves to a new §22

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — verified at HEAD: `resolve_launch_executable` carries the `backend` parameter (`reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:1184-1189`) and its only three production callers pass no `backend` (`dispatch.py:3233`, `dispatch_sessions.py:1332`, `:1849`); `_persisted_worker_environment` (`dispatch_launch.py:730`) forwards `backend_name` alone to `launch_search_path` (`:647`); `flight.py:2349` is the bare `shutil.which(command)`; both cited §20 review ids resolve (`r-20261108T205206811901` under the plan-review reports, `r-20261108T213151677264` under the crew runs). Two line pointers have drifted with later commits (`dispatch.py` 3164→3233, `dispatch_launch.py` 670→730) but every one of them is anchored on a named symbol, and the flow they describe still holds; the cited landing sha `5631154f78` is §20's recorded run head, a `docs(evidence)` commit whose own record names the code revision that carries the input (`bb92bb806b`).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §21 names a new test with two cases, three negative controls each tied to one case ("dropping the backend from the composed-plan call refuses the first case at plan build", "forwarding only the backend name … leaves the directory out of the persisted PATH", "a bare `shutil.which` fails the second case"), a named importer-population delta against base and the ruff floor; every control is falsifiable and none is a suite that would pass on unfixed code. The gate exercises a fresh cli dispatch only, which is what the finding below is about.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gate logs go "under the run directory", a durable crew run directory, not a scratchpad or node-local temp.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `tests/test_every_backend_reader_searches_the_declared_path.py` names the mechanism, and no proposed symbol, comment or filename carries a plan label, section number, ticket number or version tag.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the root cause matches the evidence it cites, but the mechanism it prescribes for the persisted environment cannot run on the resume path it also means to cover; see the finding below.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the three readers (§21's three named sites) are one invariant, "a declared search path reaches every reader", with one test file and one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` declares `s21` on `a-dispatch-returns-without-its-worker#s20` (plan.html:29), §20 stands `done` with its recorded head at `5631154f78`, so the wait is discharged and §21 declares no edge that points elsewhere.
